hero.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as approval ratings hit new lows
hero.teaser: President Trump will sit for an interview on NBC's Meet the Press following a week of declining approval ratings and tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a challenging week that has seen his approval ratings decline and his relationships with Senate Republicans deteriorate publicly. The interview comes as midterm elections approach and the president faces escalating political pressure.

Trump's approval ratings have reached concerning levels. According to Gallup polling data, his second-term approval rating fell to 36 percent in December, marking one of the lowest figures the polling organization has recorded. This represents a significant drop from his 47 percent approval rating when he began his second term.

The decline in approval ratings has occurred amid disagreements on multiple fronts, including economic challenges and policy disputes with members of his own party. Growing friction with Senate Republicans has become increasingly visible to the public, creating additional obstacles for the president as his party prepares for the midterm campaign season.

Trump has shown considerable frustration with polling organizations that report unfavorable numbers about his popularity. In January, after the New York Times released a poll showing his approval rating at 40 percent, down three percentage points since September 2025, Trump threatened to expand an existing defamation lawsuit against the newspaper. In a post on Truth Social, he wrote that the Times Siena Poll "will be added to my lawsuit against The Failing New York Times."

The New York Times defended the integrity of its polling work in response to Trump's criticism. Charlie Stadtlander, a spokesperson for the newspaper, stated: "President Trump likes polls that appear favorable to him and dislikes polls that do not. But whether a poll is good or bad for the president has no bearing on our methodology." The Times noted that its polling methodology has been widely recognized for its rigor.

Meanwhile, Gallup announced this week that it will cease tracking presidential approval ratings after nearly nine decades. The polling organization, which has measured presidential approval since Harry Truman's administration, said the decision reflects "an evolution in how Gallup focuses its public research and thought leadership." A company spokesperson emphasized that the choice was based solely on the organization's research priorities and goals, not external pressure.

The Gallup Presidential Approval Rating has served as one of the most influential measures of public opinion regarding presidential performance throughout American history. The data has captured significant moments, including George W. Bush's 90 percent approval rating in the days following the 9/11 attacks.

Trump's upcoming appearance on Meet the Press will provide an opportunity for the president to address the political headwinds he currently faces. The interview occurs at a critical moment as his administration navigates both internal party tensions and declining public support.

cards.headline: US forces shoot down Iranian drones in Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The US military shot down two Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz, according to American officials. The incident represents another escalation in the region as both nations exchange strikes while ceasefire negotiations remain stalled.

The exchange of military fire tested the fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran. According to reports, Iran launched missiles and drones toward the strategic waterway, which handles roughly a fifth of global oil trade. The Trump administration has ramped up pressure on Iran to reach a deal to end the conflict.

Iran responded to the US action by targeting American bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. Tehran accused the United States of violating the ceasefire agreement following the American strikes. Both sides have traded accusations over responsibility for the breakdown in peace talks aimed at reducing tensions in the Persian Gulf.

The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. Its narrow width makes it a critical chokepoint for oil tankers traveling from Gulf states to global markets. Any military activity in the strait raises immediate concerns about the security of commercial shipping and energy supplies.

The Pentagon confirmed that US forces engaged the Iranian drones to protect commercial traffic passing through the strait. Military officials described the action as defensive and necessary to ensure the safety of international shipping. The incident underscores the difficulty of maintaining stability in the region while both sides pursue conflicting strategic objectives.

American forces have maintained a military presence in the region to protect shipping lanes and support Gulf allies. Iranian officials have characterized US military operations in the area as provocations that undermine diplomatic efforts and increase tensions in the Middle East.

According to reports, the US government is considering using frozen Iranian assets to help Gulf allies recover from damages sustained during Iranian attacks. Treasury Department officials have indicated plans to make Iranian funds available to assist US Gulf partners with repairs and reconstruction efforts related to the conflict.

The repeated testing of the ceasefire in recent weeks demonstrates how fragile the current arrangement remains. Both nations have shown willingness to engage in military action despite ongoing negotiations, creating uncertainty about the prospects for a lasting diplomatic resolution.

The situation reflects broader challenges in establishing stability across the Middle East. The narrow corridor through which global oil shipments pass remains vulnerable to disruption, making the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz a matter of international concern. As long as both sides maintain military capabilities and conflicting strategic interests in the region, the risk of further escalation continues to threaten efforts to de-escalate tensions and achieve a durable peace agreement.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Russian navy base near St Petersburg
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched hundreds of drones targeting Russian military facilities in St Petersburg as Russia hosted an international economic forum.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack on Russian military targets in St Petersburg, including a navy base and an oil terminal. The operation involved hundreds of drones and occurred while Russia was hosting a major economic forum in the city.

The timing of the strikes coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin's rejection of a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. According to the BBC's Russia editor, the drone attacks significantly overshadowed Putin's flagship economic event, which was meant to demonstrate Russian economic strength.

cards.headline: US considers using frozen Iranian assets to compensate Gulf allies
cards.teaser: The United States is weighing a plan to redirect frozen Iranian funds to Gulf states for reconstruction after damage from Iranian attacks.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department is planning to make Iranian assets available to help Gulf allies recover from damage sustained during Iranian military operations. American officials are considering using frozen Iranian funds to compensate countries in the region that were targeted in recent attacks.

The proposal would redirect Iranian assets currently held under sanctions to support reconstruction efforts in Gulf states. The move would represent a significant shift in how the United States manages frozen foreign assets and provides assistance to regional partners.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads in East Africa as US scales back involvement
cards.teaser: An Ebola outbreak is expanding in East Africa, with questions about whether China will fill a gap left by reduced US engagement.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in central Africa could reach catastrophic levels comparable to the 2014-2016 West African epidemic that killed over 11,000 people, according to modeling by US health officials. The CDC has published computer projections ranging from 10,000 to more than 20,000 cases, warning the outbreak could follow a "dangerous trajectory."

As the United States reduces its global health security presence, international health officials are working to contain the virus. The evolving response raises questions about which countries will assume leadership roles in combating the outbreak.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping visits North Korea
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping is making a rare trip to North Korea as Pyongyang calls US denuclearization efforts an anachronistic dream.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is traveling to North Korea next week, marking his first visit since 2019. Both countries announced the trip on Friday, a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility for producing nuclear fuel.

The visit underscores China's central role as North Korea's most important ally and economic lifeline. It comes as North Korea continues to reject American calls for denuclearization, characterizing such demands as outdated and unrealistic.

cards.headline: Armenia votes as Russia pressures pro-Western government
cards.teaser: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeks a third term amid Russian pressure and declining domestic support.
cards.body:
Armenia is holding elections as Russia exerts pressure on the country's pro-Western government. Incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is seeking a third term despite facing falling support at home and mounting tensions with Moscow.

The vote takes place as Armenia has sought closer ties with Western nations, a shift that has drawn opposition from Russia. Pashinyan's government has navigated competing pressures from Moscow and the West while managing domestic challenges to his leadership.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi party member reaches mayoral runoff in German town
cards.teaser: A candidate from a neo-Nazi party has advanced to a mayoral runoff in a small German town, a first since the fall of the Third Reich.
cards.body:
A member of a neo-Nazi party has reached the runoff election for mayor in a small town in eastern Germany. German voters have historically rejected mayoral candidates from neo-Nazi parties since the end of World War II, making the advancement a significant departure from past voting patterns.

The runoff election is scheduled for this week in the eastern German town. The candidate's advancement has raised concerns about the growing appeal of far-right political movements in parts of the country.

hero.headline: 12 people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
hero.body:
At least 12 people were wounded in a shooting near a street festival in Toledo, Ohio, according to authorities. Police say the incident appears to have involved two people firing weapons at each other rather than targeting the crowd indiscriminately.

The shooting took place on Saturday near the community festival location. Victims were transported to nearby hospitals following the incident. Two of the wounded were reported to be in critical condition, according to Toledo deputy police chief Joe Heffernan.

"It appeared there were at least two people firing weapons who were probably shooting at each other," Heffernan said.

Law enforcement launched a search for the suspects involved in the shooting. Police are working to identify and locate the individuals responsible for opening fire near the festival grounds. The investigation into what prompted the gunfire is ongoing.

The victims range in age from 14 to 61 years old, demonstrating the broad impact of the shooting on the community. Details about the specific injuries sustained by those shot or their current medical conditions were not immediately released by authorities.

The shooting represents another instance of gun violence occurring at a public gathering in an American community. The incident disrupted what was intended to be a community celebration, forcing emergency responders to the scene.

Police have continued their investigation to determine the full circumstances surrounding the shooting and to apprehend those responsible for the gunfire. Authorities are urging anyone with information about the incident to come forward.

cards.headline: Federal probe launched into California election administration
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California announced an investigation into election administration as millions of ballots remain uncounted.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice has sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California continues counting millions of ballots from primary elections. The move comes amid delays in results for the governor's race, as well as contests for LA mayor and Congress.

President Trump has repeatedly claimed without evidence that California Democrats are "rigging" the election results. State officials have rejected these allegations. The delay in ballot counting has contributed to the spread of misinformation about California's election integrity.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump issued a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
President Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served nearly two years in prison for insider trading. Buyer was convicted of making illegal stock trades based on confidential information while working as a consultant and lobbyist after leaving Congress. He was sentenced to 22 months in prison in 2023 and ordered to forfeit over $350,000 in illegal gains plus pay a $10,000 fine. He was released in 2025.

The pardon comes as Trump's administration emphasizes tackling fraud in Democratic-led states, while the president has repeatedly used his pardon power to excuse financial crimes by Republicans.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as Raman closes gap with Pratt
cards.teaser: New vote tallies show Nithya Raman narrowing the gap with Kevin Pratt in the Los Angeles mayoral primary as counting continues.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman has closed the gap with Kevin Pratt in the Los Angeles mayoral race as additional votes are tallied. The latest results show Pratt's lead over Raman continuing to erode, though Mayor Karen Bass maintains her lead in the overall race. Millions of ballots remain to be counted across California.

The shifting vote totals have intensified scrutiny of the slow counting process in Los Angeles. Voters are awaiting final results in both the mayoral race and the California governor's race. The prolonged count has drawn attention to ballot processing procedures in the state's largest city.

cards.headline: SoFi Stadium workers authorize strike ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: Workers at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles voted to authorize a strike as negotiations continue before the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
Workers at SoFi Stadium have voted to authorize a strike ahead of the World Cup. The union representing the workers is in negotiations with the hospitality group operating the Los Angeles stadium and FIFA.

The strike authorization empowers union leadership to call a walkout if negotiations break down. Talks between the parties are scheduled to continue Monday. The stadium will host World Cup matches, making the labor dispute's timing significant.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes European migration policy in Normandy speech
cards.teaser: U.S. Defense Secretary Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary speech to attack Europe over migration, describing it as a beach invasion.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered a speech in Normandy during D-Day commemorations, 82 years after Allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. In his remarks, he attacked European migration policies, using an "invasion" metaphor related to beaches.

The speech marked an unusual departure from traditional D-Day anniversary events, which typically center on honoring the Allied military effort and celebrating transatlantic partnership. Hegseth's choice to critique European domestic policy at this particular venue and occasion drew notable attention.

cards.headline: British Prime Minister Starmer says he will contest any leadership challenge
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Keir Starmer told supporters he would fight any Labour leadership contest after Andy Burnham indicated he would run.
cards.body:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has told supporters he will fight any potential Labour Party leadership contest. His stance hardened after Andy Burnham indicated he would enter if such a contest occurred.

The exchange reflects internal tensions within Labour as Starmer leads the party while serving as prime minister.

hero.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 in worst weekly drop since FTX collapse
hero.body:
Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 this week, marking its lowest level since October 2024 and capping the worst weekly performance for major cryptocurrencies since the FTX exchange collapsed in late 2022. Ether and other digital assets also posted sharp declines, erasing gains made since the November 2024 presidential election.

The selloff accelerated throughout the week as investors pulled back from riskier assets amid broader market uncertainty. Bitcoin traded near its 2026 low, while Ether similarly suffered steep losses. The synchronized decline across cryptocurrency markets reflected a sharp reversal from the optimism that had driven prices higher in late 2024 and early 2025.

The magnitude of the weekly drop drew comparisons to the November 2022 FTX crisis, when the collapse of one of the world's largest cryptocurrency exchanges triggered a cascade of selling across digital asset markets. While this week's decline stemmed from different factors, the percentage losses approached those seen during that turbulent period.

The retreat represents a significant setback for cryptocurrency markets, which had rallied following the 2024 election on expectations of more favorable regulatory treatment. Bitcoin had climbed substantially in the months after November, but has now given back those gains and more. The decline wiped out billions in market value across the cryptocurrency sector.

Market analysts pointed to multiple factors contributing to the selloff, though the sources did not specify particular catalysts. The speed and severity of the decline caught many investors off guard, with trading volumes elevated as holders moved to exit positions. The drop below $60,000 for Bitcoin marked a psychological threshold that had held for much of the past year and a half, raising questions about whether further declines could follow.

cards.headline: US states prepare lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros
cards.teaser: Multiple state attorneys general are preparing legal action to prevent Paramount's proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery.
cards.body:
A coalition of US state governments is preparing to file a lawsuit aimed at blocking Paramount's planned acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, according to sources familiar with the matter. The states are moving to challenge what would be one of the largest media mergers in history, valued at approximately $110 billion.

Paramount has indicated willingness to sell some of its children's channels to address concerns from European Union regulators about market concentration. Industry workers held a town hall opposing the merger, with some characterizing it as harmful to the American entertainment industry. A Paramount lawyer responded to merger opponents, claiming some held antisemitic views, escalating tensions around the proposed deal.

cards.headline: SpaceX's proposed $1.8 trillion IPO faces skepticism over market capacity
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's plans for a SpaceX public offering at a $1.8 trillion valuation are drawing doubts about whether financial markets can absorb such a large deal.
cards.body:
Wall Street analysts are questioning whether SpaceX's planned initial public offering can succeed at its anticipated $1.8 trillion valuation. The proposed offering would be the largest IPO in history by a significant margin, raising concerns about market capacity to handle such a massive deal.

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon hosted an event focused on SpaceX that drew significant investor interest. The company's valuation and IPO plans have generated substantial attention in financial markets, though questions remain about execution. Other space industry companies continue to operate as publicly traded alternatives for investors seeking exposure to the sector.

cards.headline: Pfizer's monthly obesity drug shows similar side effects to existing treatments
cards.teaser: Pfizer released midstage trial data for its once-monthly obesity injection, showing a side-effect profile comparable to Novo Nordisk's Wegovy.
cards.body:
Pfizer disclosed results from a midstage clinical trial of its monthly obesity treatment berobenatide, which showed side effects similar to those of existing weight-loss drugs like Wegovy. The company is positioning itself in the growing market for obesity medications with a less frequent dosing schedule than current weekly injections.

The detailed trial data suggests Pfizer's drug candidate continues to show promise as the company seeks to compete in the weight-loss pharmaceutical market. Pfizer is betting on obesity drugs to drive growth over the next decade. The move toward monthly rather than weekly injections represents an industry trend aimed at improving patient convenience and adherence to treatment regimens.

cards.headline: Major companies invest in training programs to address skilled trades shortage
cards.teaser: Large US businesses are funding education initiatives to develop mechanics and electricians as demand for skilled tradespeople outpaces supply.
cards.body:
Major corporations are spending on training programs to develop workers in skilled trades as the United States faces a shortage of mechanics, electricians, and other technical professionals. The investment comes as industries struggle to fill positions requiring specialized technical skills.

A recent report found that the collision repair industry's technician pipeline fills only 42 percent of current demand. Ford's CEO warned that the blue-collar worker shortage could have broader economic consequences for consumers. The gap between available workers and industry needs has prompted companies to take direct action in workforce development rather than relying solely on traditional educational institutions.

cards.headline: WWE shareholder lawsuit trial removed from court calendar
cards.teaser: A trial involving WWE shareholders over the company's merger has been canceled and taken off the court schedule.
cards.body:
A lawsuit brought by WWE shareholders related to the company's merger has had its trial date canceled and removed from the court calendar. The cancellation spares WWE executives, including former chairman Vince McMahon, from immediate courtroom proceedings.

The case had been scheduled to go to trial, with shareholders challenging aspects of WWE's merger transaction. The removal from the calendar represents a development in ongoing litigation over the deal. Additional details about the case had emerged as it was preparing for trial before the cancellation.

cards.headline: Executives deploy AI twins to handle meetings and messages
cards.teaser: Corporate leaders and academics are using artificial intelligence versions of themselves to answer questions and attend meetings.
cards.body:
CEOs and Harvard professors are adopting AI-powered digital twins as a productivity tool. The technology allows these individuals to delegate routine communications and meeting attendance to AI systems trained to respond in their manner.

The trend represents a new application of artificial intelligence in executive time management. Proponents view AI twins as a way to handle increasing communication demands while focusing on higher-priority tasks. The technology raises questions about the boundaries between personal engagement and automated delegation in professional settings.

hero.headline: OpenAI introduces Lockdown Mode to block prompt injection attacks on sensitive data
hero.body:
OpenAI has introduced Lockdown Mode, a new security feature designed to protect sensitive information from prompt injection attacks. The tool aims to reduce the risk that confidential data becomes exposed when bad actors attempt to manipulate ChatGPT through carefully constructed prompts.

Prompt injection attacks represent a growing security challenge as businesses increasingly integrate AI tools into workflows handling proprietary or sensitive information. These attacks work by embedding hidden instructions within user input that can trick AI systems into ignoring their safety guidelines. By embedding malicious commands in seemingly innocent requests, attackers can potentially extract confidential details that the AI was designed to protect.

The company acknowledges that Lockdown Mode does not eliminate vulnerability to prompt injection techniques entirely. However, the feature significantly reduces the likelihood that sensitive data gets shared during such attacks. OpenAI designed the tool primarily for enterprise and business users who deploy ChatGPT in environments where data security is critical, such as handling customer information, internal communications, or proprietary research.

Lockdown Mode represents OpenAI's response to security challenges that have intensified alongside widespread AI adoption. As organizations move beyond experimental phases into production deployments, the risk of data breaches through AI systems has become a serious concern. The feature provides stronger controls for companies integrating ChatGPT into sensitive operations.

The company has not disclosed specific technical details about how Lockdown Mode works or how it differs from existing safety measures built into ChatGPT. This lack of transparency means users cannot fully understand what protections the feature provides or what its limitations might be.

OpenAI's move aligns with broader industry efforts to address vulnerabilities specific to large language models. Researchers have demonstrated multiple sophisticated techniques for extracting training data or bypassing content restrictions through advanced prompting methods. As AI systems become more embedded in business operations, the security landscape continues to evolve, with new attack vectors regularly discovered.

The introduction of Lockdown Mode signals that OpenAI recognizes the tension between making AI tools useful for businesses and ensuring they remain secure against exploitation. While the feature addresses one category of security threat, organizations deploying ChatGPT must still implement comprehensive security strategies that extend beyond individual software features.

The availability and specific requirements for accessing Lockdown Mode remain unclear. Organizations interested in enhanced protections for sensitive data should contact OpenAI directly to understand whether the feature suits their particular security needs and operational requirements.

cards.headline: Apple prepares major Siri overhaul and AI updates for WWDC developer conference
cards.teaser: Apple is expected to announce significant improvements to its Siri assistant and Apple Intelligence platform at its annual developer conference.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to unveil a major revamp of Siri alongside updates to its Apple Intelligence platform at the Worldwide Developers Conference. The announcements will come as part of the iOS 27 launch, with seven new iPhone features anticipated. The conference represents a significant moment for CEO Tim Cook, as it marks his final WWDC as chief executive.

The updates focus on improving Siri's capabilities and expanding Apple's AI offerings. The company has faced pressure to compete with advances from rivals in artificial intelligence and voice assistant technology. The developer conference will provide the first look at how Apple plans to integrate these improvements into its ecosystem.

cards.headline: Scientists discover three-foot scorpion with six-inch pincers from 415 million years ago
cards.teaser: Fossils reveal the largest scorpion ever discovered, a creature the size of a baseball bat that lived during the Devonian period.
cards.body:
Paleontologists identified fossils of the largest scorpion ever documented, measuring over three feet in length with pincers reaching six inches. The creature lived approximately 415 million years ago during the Devonian period, when it ruled ancient Britain. The Natural History Museum confirmed the discovery based on fossil analysis.

The scorpion, comparable in size to a full-grown German Shepherd or baseball bat, represents one of the most imposing arthropods to have existed. The Devonian period saw numerous giant invertebrates thriving in marine and coastal environments before the evolution of large land predators.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain announced with allegations of AI-generated content in trailer
cards.teaser: Developer Shift Up revealed Blood Rain, the sequel to Stellar Blade, but the announcement trailer faces scrutiny over potential use of generative AI.
cards.body:
Shift Up officially announced Blood Rain, the sequel to action game Stellar Blade, with a reveal trailer showcasing combat mechanics and large-scale cityscapes. The trailer highlighted the game's stylish combat system and expansive environments. However, observers have alleged that portions of the reveal trailer appear to contain content created using generative AI technology.

The allegations center on specific visual elements in the trailer that critics claim show characteristics typical of AI-generated imagery. Shift Up has not addressed the claims. The controversy emerges as the gaming industry grapples with debates over the appropriate use of AI in game development and marketing materials.

cards.headline: Telescope facility to begin decade-long survey of millions of undiscovered solar system objects
cards.teaser: A new astronomical facility will start operations within months to catalog millions of previously unseen objects within our solar system.
cards.body:
A new telescope facility will begin a decade-long survey to identify millions of objects in the solar system that have never been observed. The survey is scheduled to start within months, marking a significant expansion in our ability to map nearby space. The project aims to catalog asteroids, comets, and other bodies that have remained undetected.

The facility will systematically scan the sky to build a comprehensive inventory of solar system objects. The survey's findings will improve understanding of the solar system's composition and could identify objects that pose potential risks to Earth.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference for distributing journal reprints
cards.teaser: Conference organizers ejected multiple scientists, including a journal editor and former association president, for handing out academic reprints.
cards.body:
Several prominent scientists were ejected from a diabetes conference for distributing journal reprints. Those removed included Steven Kahn, editor-in-chief of an American Diabetes Association journal, and Desmond Schatz, a former ADA president.

The incident has raised questions about conference policies and the boundaries around sharing published research at academic events.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors announces Nintendo Switch 2 version and new downloadable content
cards.teaser: The indie game Vampire Survivors is coming to the next-generation Nintendo console with additional content planned.
cards.body:
Poncle has confirmed that Vampire Survivors is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. The studio also revealed plans to open a Japan-based studio under the leadership of El Shaddai creator Sawaki Takeyasu, marking an expansion of the indie developer's international operations.

The developer announced new downloadable content called Legacy of the Blood Moon, described as an evil twin expansion. These announcements reflect poncle's growth strategy as it broadens the game's platform reach and content library.

hero.headline: Marner scores Stanley Cup Final hat trick in second period as Hurricanes fall in double overtime
hero.body:
Mitch Marner made NHL history by recording the fastest hat trick ever in a Stanley Cup Final game, but it was not enough to prevent the Vegas Golden Knights from escaping with a 5-4 double-overtime victory over the Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night.

Shea Theodore scored the game-winner at 5:38 of the second overtime period, his goal deflecting off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate to secure Vegas a 2-1 series lead. The Golden Knights had squandered a four-goal advantage before Theodore's heroics ended the marathon contest.

Marner's performance in the second period was the highlight of an otherwise dramatic game for Vegas. His three goals in a single period marked the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history, giving the Golden Knights a commanding advantage early in the match. The pace and efficiency of Marner's scoring set a new benchmark for the championship series.

However, the Hurricanes mounted an impressive comeback that nearly rewrote the outcome. Carolina systematically erased Vegas's four-goal lead and forced the game into overtime, refusing to concede despite facing a historic individual performance from their opponent. The first overtime period failed to produce a winner, pushing the game into a second extra frame where Theodore eventually ended the contest.

The loss puts Carolina in a difficult position as the series shifts focus. The Hurricanes now trail 2-1 with the remainder of the series returning to other venues. They must regroup quickly to avoid falling deeper into a deficit against a Vegas team that has proven capable of closing out tight contests.

Both teams demonstrated the intensity expected in championship hockey throughout the evening. The game featured multiple lead changes and strong performances on both sides, making it one of the most dramatic contests in recent Stanley Cup Final history. The Hurricanes showed resilience by fighting back from such a significant deficit, but ultimately came up short in the extra periods.

Vegas's ability to hold on despite losing a substantial lead will likely boost confidence heading forward, though the team's vulnerability in that final stretch may concern coach Bruce Cassidy. For Carolina, the comeback effort showed the team has the character to compete with Vegas, but they will need to find a way to eliminate the early deficits that have plagued them through the first three games.

Marner's historic achievement will be remembered as a significant moment in Cup Final lore regardless of the series outcome. The feat of scoring three goals in a single Final period had never been accomplished before, making his performance historically significant even in a losing effort for Vegas.

cards.headline: Korda shares lead at US Women's Open as Hull surges into contention
cards.teaser: Nelly Korda shot a four-under 67 to move into a share of the lead after the third round, while England's Charley Hull fired a 65 to climb the leaderboard.
cards.body:
Nelly Korda carded a four-under par 67 in the third round of the US Women's Open, moving into a share of the lead heading into the final round. 

England's Charley Hull surged up the leaderboard with a five-under 65, positioning herself as a contender for the title as the tournament heads into its concluding day.

cards.headline: Bonfim defeats Muhammad in main event at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Gabriel Bonfim dominated Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas, winning the main event.
cards.body:
Gabriel Bonfim defeated Belal Muhammad in the main event at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas. Bonfim controlled the fight throughout, earning a decisive victory over Muhammad in the welterweight bout.

The win represents a significant result for Bonfim at UFC Vegas 118. Muhammad, a ranked welterweight contender, was unable to overcome Bonfim's performance during the scheduled rounds.

cards.headline: Brazil defeats USWNT 2-1 in international friendly
cards.teaser: Brazil beat the United States women's national team 2-1 in a friendly match in Sao Paulo.
cards.body:
Brazil defeated the United States women's national team 2-1 in an international friendly at Sao Paulo on Saturday. Sophia Wilson scored in her first US appearance since 2024, but Brazil quickly answered with two goals in three minutes to secure the victory.

The loss marks the start of the USWNT's World Cup cycle as the team prepares for the 2027 tournament. The Americans had scheduled a pair of matches in Brazil as part of their preparation for the upcoming competition.

cards.headline: Mitchell secures submission victory in final seconds at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Bryce Mitchell scored a submission win in the closing seconds of his bout against Santiago Luna at UFC Vegas 118.
cards.body:
Bryce Mitchell defeated Santiago Luna with a dramatic submission in the final seconds of their fight at UFC Fight Night 278. Mitchell secured the victory just before the final bell, ending the contest with a late finish.

The win came on short notice for Mitchell, who took on the undefeated Luna in a changed matchup. Mitchell's grappling prowess proved decisive as he capitalized on a late opportunity to force the submission.

cards.headline: Elliott to lead field at Michigan International Speedway after NASCAR qualifying
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott earned the pole position for the NASCAR race at Michigan International Speedway, leading Hendrick Motorsports to the front of the starting grid.
cards.body:
Chase Elliott will start from pole position at Michigan International Speedway after winning the qualifying session. Elliott's performance puts Hendrick Motorsports at the front of the field heading into the race weekend.

The qualifying results set the starting order for the upcoming race at Michigan. Elliott's pole position gives him a strategic advantage as NASCAR competition continues at the track.

cards.headline: Scotland defeats Bolivia in final World Cup warmup match
cards.teaser: Scotland beat Bolivia decisively in their last preparation game before the World Cup begins.
cards.body:
Scotland dismantled Bolivia in their final World Cup warmup match, delivering a dominant performance that has given the team considerable confidence heading into the tournament. The victory comes ahead of their first World Cup appearance in 28 years.

Manager Steve Clarke's side showed ruthlessness and efficiency that suggests they could emerge from the group phase for the first time in Scotland's international history. The convincing win has eased concerns about their upcoming match against Haiti next weekend, with the team appearing to be in excellent form as they prepare for their opening game.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso Actor, Dies at 72
hero.body:
British actor Anthony Head, best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72 from complications due to pneumonia. His daughters Emily and Daisy Head confirmed he passed away peacefully, surrounded by family.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said in a statement.

Head's most iconic role was as the mentor and father figure to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character throughout Buffy's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. In a tribute posted on Instagram, Gellar opened with a quote from her character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She continued, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father was a documentary filmmaker who founded Verity Films, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother was also an actor, best known for his lead role in the 1971 film Sunday Bloody Sunday.

Head began his professional career on stage, starring in a 1978 West End revival of Godspell alongside Su Pollard. Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, he appeared in various productions including the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988 and a 1990 production of The Rocky Horror Show as Dr. Frank-N-Furter. He also took roles in films including a 1981 adaptation of Lady Chatterley's Lover and 1987's A Prayer for the Dying with Bob Hoskins and Liam Neeson.

In the early 1980s, Head sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and was featured on their 1986 debut album. He became widely recognized in the UK and US for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements, which portrayed a slow-burn courtship between a British couple.

While filming Buffy in Los Angeles, Head remained committed to his family in England. He told The Guardian that he would return home every three or four weeks whenever the production schedule allowed, spending considerable money on airfares to maintain those connections.

After Buffy ended, Head took a recurring role in the BBC sketch show Little Britain and appeared in the BBC production of Merlin. In recent years, he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion in the Apple TV series Ted Lasso, which introduced him to new audiences and earned praise for his on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

Head's daughters noted that his legacy will live on through the shows he worked on and the audiences who loved them.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily With Elton John Performance
cards.teaser: Pop star Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner married in Sicily with Elton John performing at the ceremony.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and Callum Turner held their wedding in Sicily, with Elton John serenading the couple with a performance of Your Song, according to Vanity Fair. The ceremony took place in Italy and featured what multiple outlets described as vintage glamour.

The wedding also took place in London, with The New York Times noting the couple brought vintage glamor to their London nuptials. Vogue reported that the bride wore leather for one of her wedding looks in Italy. The event divided opinion in Palermo, with The Guardian quoting a local saying they could understand the disruption if it was for the pope. E! News reported the Italian wedding included a nod to the couple's first meeting.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Debuts Duet With The Cure's Robert Smith at Primavera Sound
cards.teaser: Olivia Rodrigo premiered a new song featuring The Cure's Robert Smith during a surprise performance at Primavera Sound festival.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo brought Robert Smith of The Cure on stage at the Primavera Sound festival to debut their duet What's Wrong With Me from her upcoming album, which releases in less than a week. Variety described the collaboration as one of pop's best-kept secrets of 2026.

Rodrigo performed a surprise set at the festival, with Yahoo reporting she rocked Primavera Sound 2026 with the unexpected appearance. Billboard and Consequence of Sound both covered the live debut of the duet. Forbes noted that the newest song breaks a longstanding tradition for Rodrigo, though the source material does not specify what tradition was broken.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Opens Music Center in New Jersey
cards.teaser: Bruce Springsteen opened the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music at Monmouth University with concerts featuring Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy.
cards.body:
Bruce Springsteen opened his music center with guitars, according to The New York Times. The Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music opened at Monmouth University on June 13, as announced on brucespringsteen.net.

Springsteen performed at a Music America concert that featured Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy, according to Rolling Stone and Yahoo. The Asbury Park Press reported that the concert gave fans something to talk about. The star-studded event marked the launch of the new center dedicated to American music.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Loses Lawsuit Against Musician Who Canceled Over Trump Name Dispute
cards.teaser: A judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against musician Chuck Redd, who canceled a concert after a dispute over naming the venue after Trump.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center lost a legal case against a musician who canceled a performance following a dispute over the Trump name, according to The New York Times. Judge dismissed the lawsuit the Kennedy Center filed against Chuck Redd, as reported by WUSA9 and The Guardian.

The Washington Post and Washingtonian both reported that Redd canceled his concert after the venue underwent a name change involving Trump. The judge sided with the musician and threw out the Kennedy Center's suit. The case centered on whether Redd was within his rights to cancel the performance based on the naming dispute.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Thanks Supporters After 60 Minutes Firing
cards.teaser: Former 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley posted a message thanking fans for their support after being fired by the show's new executive producer.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley took to Instagram to thank supporters following his firing from 60 Minutes by executive producer Nick Bilton. In his statement, Pelley accused CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting.

Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes built its decades-long success as America's number-one program through integrity, quality, and humanity in storytelling. His firing sparked criticism from industry figures, including Sarah Safer, daughter of longtime correspondent Morley Safer, who condemned what she described as the erosion of the program's journalistic standards under new management.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Begins Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: Ariana Grande returned to touring after more than six years with the opening night of her Eternal Sunshine tour in Oakland.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande kicked off her Eternal Sunshine tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday night, marking her return to touring after a six-and-a-half-year break. The opening night featured performances from her Eternal Sunshine album.

Variety covered the concert and published the complete setlist from the show, with a full review to follow.

hero.headline: Trump to appear on Meet the Press as approval ratings hit new lows
hero.teaser: President Trump will sit for an interview on NBC's Meet the Press following a week of declining approval ratings and tensions with Senate Republicans.
hero.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press on Sunday following a challenging week that has seen his approval ratings decline and his relationships with Senate Republicans deteriorate publicly. The interview comes as midterm elections approach and the president faces escalating political pressure.

Trump's approval ratings have reached concerning levels. According to Gallup polling data, his second-term approval rating fell to 36 percent in December, marking one of the lowest figures the polling organization has recorded. This represents a significant drop from his 47 percent approval rating when he began his second term.

The decline in approval ratings has occurred amid disagreements on multiple fronts, including economic challenges and policy disputes with members of his own party. Growing friction with Senate Republicans has become increasingly visible to the public, creating additional obstacles for the president as his party prepares for the midterm campaign season.

Trump has shown considerable frustration with polling organizations that report unfavorable numbers about his popularity. In January, after the New York Times released a poll showing his approval rating at 40 percent, down three percentage points since September 2025, Trump threatened to expand an existing defamation lawsuit against the newspaper. In a post on Truth Social, he wrote that the Times Siena Poll "will be added to my lawsuit against The Failing New York Times."

The New York Times defended the integrity of its polling work in response to Trump's criticism. Charlie Stadtlander, a spokesperson for the newspaper, stated: "President Trump likes polls that appear favorable to him and dislikes polls that do not. But whether a poll is good or bad for the president has no bearing on our methodology." The Times noted that its polling methodology has been widely recognized for its rigor.

Meanwhile, Gallup announced this week that it will cease tracking presidential approval ratings after nearly nine decades. The polling organization, which has measured presidential approval since Harry Truman's administration, said the decision reflects "an evolution in how Gallup focuses its public research and thought leadership." A company spokesperson emphasized that the choice was based solely on the organization's research priorities and goals, not external pressure.

The Gallup Presidential Approval Rating has served as one of the most influential measures of public opinion regarding presidential performance throughout American history. The data has captured significant moments, including George W. Bush's 90 percent approval rating in the days following the 9/11 attacks.

Trump's upcoming appearance on Meet the Press will provide an opportunity for the president to address the political headwinds he currently faces. The interview occurs at a critical moment as his administration navigates both internal party tensions and declining public support.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office has opened an investigation into election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The U.S. attorney's office in Los Angeles announced Saturday that it has launched an investigation into alleged election fraud in California's elections. The probe comes as vote counting continues in the state's primary races.

The investigation follows claims by President Trump and other conservatives about irregularities in California's vote-counting process. Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy joined in criticizing the state's counting procedures, saying California voters were losing faith in the process as results continue to trickle in from Tuesday's primary.

cards.headline: Pence says Jan. 6 rioters pardoned by Trump should not receive compensation
cards.teaser: Former Vice President Pence said rioters who assaulted police or vandalized property during the Jan. 6 Capitol attack should not be pardoned or compensated.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that individuals who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or disrupted the certification of the 2020 presidential election during the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol attack should not receive pardons from President Trump. Speaking on HBO's Real Time, Pence said these rioters should never get a dime.

Pence's comments represent a continued break with Trump over the events of Jan. 6. The former vice president was presiding over the certification of electoral votes when rioters stormed the Capitol building. Trump has granted pardons to some individuals involved in the attack.

---

Note: The additional source material provided is about New York's datacenter ban and is unrelated to the Pence/Jan. 6 story. Per your instructions, I am returning the original card text unchanged.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of June.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of June. Krishnan, a tech investor, has been a key figure in the Trump administration's efforts to develop AI policy.

Krishnan played a central role in formulating strategic plans for President Trump's AI initiatives. His departure comes as the administration continues to shape its approach to artificial intelligence regulation and development.

The White House has not announced a replacement for Krishnan. His exit marks a shift in the administration's AI policy team as the technology continues to advance rapidly and draw increased attention from lawmakers and regulators.

The timing of Krishnan's departure coincides with ongoing debates in Washington about how to balance innovation in AI with concerns about safety, privacy, and national security. The administration has been working to establish frameworks for AI development that maintain American competitiveness while addressing risks associated with the technology.

Krishnan's background in the tech industry brought private sector expertise to the White House AI policy discussions. His tenure focused on developing approaches that would support AI research and deployment while considering regulatory guardrails.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor in New Mexico and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Tuesday. The former Secretary of the Interior under President Biden is now positioned to compete in the general election this November.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary as votes counted
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading their respective parties in California's primary for governor as vote counting continues. Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are competing for the GOP nomination, while Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra are vying for their party's spot on the November ballot.

The race will determine who replaces Governor Gavin Newsom, who is term-limited. California uses a jungle primary system, but the results still coming in show partisan divisions at the top of the field as the state continues its multi-day counting process.

cards.headline: New York City Mayor Mamdani says Democratic Party lost focus on working people
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticized the Democratic Party for losing sight of economic issues facing working-class Americans after the 2024 presidential loss.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Saturday that the Democratic Party has lost its focus on working people as it rebuilds following its 2024 presidential election defeat. Speaking in an interview, Mamdani argued that the party has shifted away from the economic concerns of working-class Americans.

Mamdani's comments reflect ongoing debates within the Democratic Party about its future direction and messaging strategy. The party has been engaged in internal discussions about how to reconnect with voters following the presidential loss.
